source.title: PAHQ: Accelerating Automated Circuit Discovery through Mixed-Precision Inference Optimization
source.authors: Xinhai Wang; Shu Yang; Liang-Yu Wang; Lin Zhang; Huan-Yi Xie; Lijie Hu; Di Wang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates circuit-discovery fidelity on IOI using AUC-ROC and an additional faithfulness metric, and compares results across precision strategies and circuit-discovery methods. It does not reproduce the claimed 26-head circuit or test its component roles.
record.gate_note: The IOI results measure circuit-discovery fidelity under different methods and precision settings. The paper does not report the 26 head classes, their roles under patching, backup-head self-repair, or comparisons across IOI prompt variants. Table 1 and Table 6 provide aggregate results; cited findings from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper uses the Wang et al. IOI circuit as a ground-truth reference to score its own speed-up of ACDC (PAHQ) against RTN quantization and other discovery methods. It reports only how well each discovery pipeline recovers that reference (AUC-ROC) and how faithful the found circuits are. It does not examine the 26 heads, their classes or roles, backup heads, other prompt formats, or whether the circuit itself holds. Quantization degrading ACDC is a property of the tool, not a sensitivity of the IOI circuit's evaluation (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that PAHQ cuts ACDC runtime by about 80% and memory by about 30% with only slight faithfulness loss. They find that direct 8-bit RTN quantization badly degrades circuit discovery.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ACDC activation-patching circuit discovery on IOI, but adds mixed-precision quantization and evaluates method fidelity; it does not reproduce or analyze the original 26-head circuit and its roles.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported fidelity varies with precision strategy (RTN-Q versus PAHQ versus unquantized ACDC) and with the faithfulness metric. The paper does not report prompt-distribution sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 small on IOI, baseline discovery methods score AUC-ROC against the Wang et al. reference edges as follows: HISP 0.81/0.82, SP 0.83/0.81, EAP 0.83/0.83 (KL/task metric). Unaccelerated ACDC scores 0.95/0.94. This is reported only as a benchmark for PAHQ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different automated circuit-discovery methods recover the IOI reference circuit's edges with varying but substantial accuracy (AUC about 0.8–0.95).

fits_no_version.finding: Reducing ACDC's numerical precision to 8-bit RTN collapses recovery of the IOI reference circuit (AUC 0.47–0.53; Hanna faithfulness 0.27). Per-head mixed precision largely preserves it (AUC 0.89; faithfulness 0.85).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-patching circuit discovery on IOI is sensitive to numerical precision of the edge being patched.

record.problems: The paper reports aggregate fidelity metrics rather than head-level circuit roles or direct overlap of recovered circuits. It provides no uncertainty estimates. Its limitations section notes that the justification for preserving patched signals through lower-precision downstream computation is primarily empirical.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 contains further threshold- and model-specific values, but its flattened presentation and apparent mismatch with the narrative’s stated IOI example make assignment to IOI conditions uncertain; these were not extracted.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, 7 classes, their roles, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality of that circuit are not examined.
No name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis is reported.
GPT-2 medium, large and XL runs report only KL of PAHQ circuits, with no head classes or roles.
The comparison of discovery methods against the reference circuit serves only as a benchmark for the authors' method. There is no overlap or role comparison and no variation of ablation type.
The circuit's faithfulness is not varied by ablation type or prompt distribution, and the share of behaviour explained is not reported.
No per-template, per-name-order or per-name-count results are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is a method-acceleration study using the IOI circuit as ground truth (T4). Internal inconsistencies exist: PAHQ IOI AUC is 0.96/0.94 in the text but 0.89 in Table 1, and ACDC is 0.982 in Figure 1 but 0.95 in Table 1. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Table 2 and the larger-model Table 7 report only discovery-pipeline scores, not circuit structure.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not identify or test the 26 attention heads, their seven classes or roles, or faithfulness, completeness and minimality of that specific circuit.
No ablation of main name-mover heads or test of backup-head self-repair is reported.
Experiments include other models and GPT-2 sizes, but do not compare whether the same head classes and roles carry IOI or are reused for other tasks.
The paper compares circuit-discovery methods using edge-classification AUC-ROC, not direct circuit overlap or head-role equivalence; it does not vary ablation types.
The study varies precision strategy and reports two faithfulness metrics, but does not test prompt-distribution sensitivity or the claimed circuit’s share of the model’s IOI behaviour.
The IOI dataset contains varied names and contexts, but the paper does not report separate results by name order, template or number of names.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Reported edge-classification AUC-ROC differs across methods, but the paper does not directly compare recovered circuit overlap or head roles (r1-r12).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI fidelity under different precision strategies and metrics
reader_labels.reason: RTN-Q and PAHQ yield lower faithfulness results than unquantized ACDC; the reported scores also vary across the AUC-ROC and Hanna et al. measures (r1-r4, r11-r15).
